To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel mutation in arginine vasopressin was identified in a kind red with autosomal dominant central diabetes insipidu s, that this mutation was found to be pathogenic in cell culture, and that the mutation was found to affect a region critical for receptor binding.

we found a new kindred with autosomally dominant neurohypophyisal diabetes insipideus, that we identified a novel mutation in a gene that encodes the hormone vasopressin, and that we demonstrated that this mutation causes cellular toxicity.

a new American kindreds with ADNDI was found to have a novel mutation in AVP-NP II, and that the mutation was predicted to result in a deletion of a phenylalanine residue in the AVP nonapeptide, a residue that is known to be critical for VP receptor binding; and that AVP-NP molecules containing this mutation were shown to cause increased rates of cell apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of autosomal dominant neurophysin diabetes insipidu.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of autosomal dominant neurophyophyseal diabetes inipidus (NDI).
the genetic basis for a disorder of fluid homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mutation of this kindred results in a loss of function in the AVP molecule.
a mutation in the VP gene, resulting in a truncated VP peptide, causes ADNDI in this kindred.
a new mutation was identified in a kind red with autosomal dominant diabetes insipidu s.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel mutation in arginine vasopressin-neurophysin II (AVP-NP II) gene, which is associated with autosomal dominant nephrogenic diabetes insipidis.
a novel AVP mutation in a kindred affected with ADNDI was identified.
we identified a novel mutation in a gene that encodes for a protein that is involved in regulating the body's fluid balance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AVP-NP II gene can be mutated in a variety of ways, and the resulting abnormal gene products can cause cellular toxicity.
we have identified a new American family with a new mutation in the AVP gene.
we have identified a new kindred with ADNI and have identified a mutation in the VP portion of the preproVP gene.
